stem: Meera has an old torch at her home in Jaipur. When she switches it on, the incandescent lamp does not glow even though the cells are new and correctly fitted. She looks through the glass bulb and sees that the thin wire inside is broken. Which statement correctly explains her observation?

options.text: The lamp cannot glow because the broken filament stops the current from passing through it.
The lamp cannot glow because the glass bulb is made of an insulating material.
The lamp can glow because the glass bulb looks whole from outside.
The lamp can glow because only the cells decide whether a lamp lights up.

teacher.key_rationale: A broken filament creates an open circuit inside the lamp, so no current flows and the lamp cannot glow; a fused lamp stays off even with good cells. Option C is the trap for students who judge by the intact glass bulb, D for those who ignore the filament, and B misattributes the fault to the glass.
